units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

frame_assumptions: Both assessments identify the same fund, the same management company proposing the same change, the same SFC, and the same applicable home regulator and home jurisdiction. Actor identity and jurisdictional applicability are premises, not established by similar labels.

The change has identical boundaries in both assessments. Its investment-objective, policy and restriction components are separately identified before deciding materiality; a change to at least one such component suffices under both supplied readings. Neither an application bundle nor the fund as a whole replaces the identified change.

Both assessments use the same complete set of product features involved in the change, including features introduced or altered. Novelty and complexity remain separate classifications; neither is inferred from the other or from unrelated fund features.

Both assessments test every home-jurisdiction requirement applicable to the identified change. Home supervision alone does not establish satisfaction. Possible local policy implications mean possible Hong Kong policy implications of that same change, without requiring realised consequences.

Applications 'concerning' and 'covering' the change refer to the same complete set of related SFC applications. Existence of any qualifying pending application controls both readings; neither reading silently selects just one application.

Both assessments fix application receipt and the absence of both approval and authorisation at the same effective-date transition. Later assessment or decision dates do not rewrite that historical fact. Preserving the existing process is interpreted as preventing bypass through this removal measure.

Both assessment dates refer to the same Gregorian calendar date for proposed reliance or implementation. The specific effective date of 28 November 2025 is assumed to govern the source's general statement of immediate effect.

Result comparison is restricted to the shared scope: a covered fund, a material post-authorisation investment change, and assessment on or after 28 November 2025. Before that date the left is outside scope, whereas the right can return false within its broader scope; those outcomes are not equated.

Post-vetting, revised-document filing and any underlying approval obligation remain distinct from eligibility for this removal. The right frame's omission of revised documents does not imply that those duties disappear.
The proposal establishes neither these premises nor legal equivalence. Referenced FAQs and the existing approval process have not been supplied substantively; their effect remains unresolved.

assumptions: Expressions use prefix notation: = is equality, or is Boolean disjunction, and date constants denote Gregorian calendar dates. Every expression refers only to the common facts defined here.

To fit eight common facts without identifying distinct predicates, fund_class and change_class are explicit integer encodings. They are bookkeeping devices, not source classifications or numerical measures. Values outside their defined domains are invalid.

The fund has one relevant domicile at assessment, so the listed continental UCITS category and UK UCITS category are mutually exclusive. fund_class is assigned only after both classifications are determined; missing evidence is not encoded as 0.

change_class encodes post-authorisation status and material investment-change status independently. Its value is assigned only when both predicates have been determined; unknown status is not encoded as false. This restricts the proposed encoding to cases where those two statuses and fund classification can be established.

Other unknown inputs remain unknown under both readings. No unknown home requirement, feature classification, possible policy implication or application history is filled with a convenient Boolean value.

The common comparison domain is (and (or (= fund_class 1) (= fund_class 2)) (= change_class 3) (>= reliance_date (date 2025-11-28))). Within that domain both results reduce to (and home_compliance (not novel_feature) (not complex_feature) (not possible_hk_policy) (not transition_pending)).

There is no unconditional equality of scope and result pairs. In particular, before 28 November 2025 the left supplies no conclusion, while the right can supply false for an otherwise in-scope change. The date condition may be moved between scope and result only under the stated shared-domain restriction.

Both original statements label true as TRUE_IS_SATISFIED, which the permitted output enum cannot express. TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT is used conditionally and solely as a positive eligibility-polarity label for satisfying this removal's modeled conditions. It does not mean overall legal compliance, legal approval or compliance with every applicable obligation. Without this restricted interpretation the output enum is not a faithful semantic label.
False within the shared scope means removal is unavailable under these models. It establishes neither prohibition nor an independently applicable prior-approval obligation.

The pending-application exclusion is a shared interpretation of preservation of the existing process, not an independently verified consequence of the missing FAQs or existing rules. All frame premises remain conditions requiring verification.

common_facts.meaning: Classification of the same identified fund at the assessment date: 1 means it is a UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands; 2 means it is a collective investment scheme domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS; 0 means neither. The categories are exclusive under the single-relevant-domicile premise. Unknown classification has no assigned code.
common_facts.name: fund_class
common_facts.unit: Categorical code 0, 1 or 2 for one identified fund; no magnitude or ordering

common_facts.meaning: Independent status encoding for the same identified change proposed by the management company: let P mean the change is a post-authorisation matter for an already SFC-authorised fund, and M mean the change is material and changes at least one investment objective, policy or restriction. Code 0 means neither; 1 means P only; 2 means M only; 3 means both. Objective, policy and restriction components are identified separately when assessing M. Unknown P or M has no assigned code.
common_facts.name: change_class
common_facts.unit: Status-pair code 0 through 3 for one identified change; not a materiality scale

common_facts.meaning: The date for which both assessments evaluate reliance on the removal measure for implementation of the same proposed change; distinct from application receipt and decision dates.
common_facts.name: reliance_date

common_facts.meaning: The identified change satisfies every home-jurisdiction requirement applicable to that change at the common assessment date, using the same jurisdiction, requirement set and affected components in both readings. Home-regulator supervision is not substituted for compliance.
common_facts.name: home_compliance
common_facts.unit: Truth value universally quantified over applicable home requirements for the identified change

common_facts.meaning: At least one product feature involved in the identified change, including a feature introduced or altered, is classified as novel under the shared assessment. Unrelated fund features are outside this quantification.
common_facts.name: novel_feature
common_facts.unit: Truth value existentially quantified over features involved in the identified change

common_facts.meaning: At least one product feature involved in the identified change, including a feature introduced or altered, is classified as complex under the shared assessment. This classification is independent of novelty.
common_facts.name: complex_feature
common_facts.unit: Truth value existentially quantified over features involved in the identified change

common_facts.meaning: The identified change may have Hong Kong policy implications under the shared assessment. This is a possibility test for the change as a whole, including its components, and requires no realised implication.
common_facts.name: possible_hk_policy
common_facts.unit: Truth value for possible local policy implications of the identified change

common_facts.meaning: There exists an application concerning or covering the identified change that the SFC received before 28 November 2025 and for which neither approval nor authorisation had been granted at the effective-date transition. All related applications are considered. False includes established absence of any such application; unknown history is not false. Subsequent passage of time does not alter this historical predicate.
common_facts.name: transition_pending
common_facts.unit: Truth value existentially quantified over related applications using receipt timing and decision status at transition
